headline: I'm a marketing generalist who likes figuring things out.
intro: I work across content, SEO, AEO, design, and marketing automation. I write, build campaigns, improve websites, and use code to automate the repetitive stuff. I'm also getting more into product marketing and GTM.
personalNote: Outside work, I brew cold brew religiously, read books, and rewatch Schitt's Creek. I don't seem to get tired of it.
essayTitle: Not everything I care about has to be useful.
essay:
I spend a fair amount of time on the internet doing absolutely nothing in particular. I'll start looking at one thing, end up somewhere completely unrelated, and before I know it, a couple of hours have passed. Usually, I'm having a good time.

Then, later in the day, I'll think about all the things I could have done instead.

I could have learnt something new, worked on an idea, or spent some time getting better at something I've been meaning to learn. I have enough things I want to do. The problem is that I don't always get around to doing them, and when I look back at how I spent my time, I wonder if I could have made better choices.

It's a strange feeling because I don't necessarily regret the time itself. I enjoyed what I was doing. I just can't always shake the feeling that I should have done something more with those hours.

I think some of it comes from having a vague idea of the person I want to become. There are things I want to learn, things I want to try, and things I want to get better at. I know these things take time, and I sometimes worry that I'm not giving them enough of it.

But there are only so many hours in a day. And not all of them are going to be spent doing something that gets me closer to where I want to be.

I don't have a problem with wanting more for myself. I like having things to look forward to and things I'm curious about. I just wonder when that feeling of needing to do more starts getting in the way of enjoying what I'm already doing.

Because sometimes I really am just having a nice afternoon, reading random things on the internet, listening to music, or getting distracted by something I probably won't remember tomorrow. I don't want to have to find a good reason for enjoying myself.

I still have days when I look back and wish I'd done more. Maybe that's not going away anytime soon. But I don't think every hour needs to be accounted for, either. I'm still figuring out how to make time for the things I want to do without feeling bad about all the other things I want to do, too.
siteSectionTitle: A home for the things I make
siteSectionCopy: I've wanted a place of my own on the internet, somewhere beyond a résumé or a collection of links. I'm slowly building it into a home for my work, writing, and whatever catches my attention along the way.
footerQuote: I dream. Sometimes I think that's the only right thing to do.
